signals.title: JPY/SEK — G10 Bilateral Theme + CB Divergence
signals.text: G10 scorecard metrics confirm broad JPY outperformance against persistent SEK weakness over the trailing week. JPY leads all G10 peers with a 1W average gain of +2.124% across 7 pairs, while SEK lags at -1.542% across 2 pairs, producing a critical 3.666% bilateral performance spread. This move defies the nominal policy carry deficit, where Riksbank at 1.75% maintains a 75bp premium over BoJ at 1.0%. The divergence reflects shifting monetary policy trajectories, as headlines signal the Bank of Japan is preparing to raise its policy rate to 1.25% at the 18 September meeting, whereas Sweden CPI prints are due at 06:00 UTC. In technical positioning, USD/SEK trades at 9.689, positioned above its SMA20 at 9.552 and SMA50 at 9.588, highlighting underlying SEK vulnerability. Trade bias: Long JPY/SEK; widening policy trajectory divergence favors continued bilateral outperformance. Catalyst: Sweden CPI release 14 Sep at 06:00 UTC. Risk: BoJ holds rate at 1.0% with dovish forward guidance on 18 Sep, triggering carry-trade re-engagement.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long Positioning
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7164, holding just below its immediate SMA20 level at 0.7168 but comfortably above its SMA50 at 0.7069 and SMA200 at 0.7003. CFTC leveraged funds positioning shows a net long stance of +48,379 contracts, sitting at the 93rd percentile of its 52-week historical range with a z-score of +1.72. The weekly change reveals an outflow of -1,871 contracts, indicating that institutional allocation growth is stalling near multi-month highs. Cash market carry remains supportive with RBA AONIA at 4.35% holding a 73bp carry advantage over Fed SOFR at 3.62%. However, 25-delta risk reversals display a mild put skew of -0.67, confirming that derivative markets are paying for downside protection rather than chasing the extended cash move. Trade bias: Neutral/range AUD/USD; upper-decile spec crowding constrains additional topside momentum. Catalyst: RBA policy meeting 29 Sep. Risk: Leveraged funds net longs break cleanly above +50k contracts alongside a daily close above the 0.7168 SMA20.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Sovereign Spread + Technical Resistance
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1601, pinned below both its 20-day moving average at 1.1630 and 200-day moving average at 1.1637, while holding above the 50-day moving average at 1.1532. Sovereign fixed income markets continue to penalize the single currency, with German 10-year Bund yields at 3.52% sitting at a 145bp discount to US 10-year Treasury yields at 4.97%. The benchmark OIS differential reflects this ongoing gap, with Fed SOFR at 3.62% maintaining a +143bp carry advantage over ECB €STR at 2.19%. Furthermore, the US yield curve operates in a bear flattener regime with 2s10s at +41.5bp, reinforcing broad dollar resilience. ECB holds at 2.65%. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; ongoing sovereign yield discount and moving-average resistance cap recoveries. Catalyst: France and Spain CPI prints 14 Sep starting at 06:45 UTC. Risk: Sustained daily close above the SMA200 at 1.1637 accompanied by a compression of the DE-US 10-year spread inside 130bp.
